Classification and constraints\n12\t- **What:** one line on the system.\n13\t- **Type:** software / infra / AI-agentic (or a mix); greenfield or brownfield; small build or not.\n14\t- **Dominant constraint:** correctness | availability | latency | cost | scale | compliance.\n15\t- **Worst failure:** the single failure that would hurt most.\n16\t\n17\t**Budgets** (only the rows that bind; add rows the system needs, such as a cutover freeze window):\n18\t\n19\t| Budget | Target | Label | Checked by |\n20\t|---|---|---|---|\n21\t| Latency | … | REQUIREMENT / BASELINE / ASSUMPTION / UNKNOWN | V… or Phase … |\n22\t| Throughput | … | … | … |\n23\t| Availability / SLO | … | … | … |\n24\t| RPO / RTO | … | … | … |\n25\t| Resource use | … | … | … |\n26\t| AI inference cost | … (AI systems only) | … | … |\n27\t| Storage cost | … | … | … |\n28\t| Operational complexity | … (e.g. services to run, on-call load) | … | … |\n29\t\n30\tAn UNKNOWN target has no number: write the missing input, who supplies it, and the phase that\n31\tneeds it. An ASSUMPTION gives its basis.\n32\t\n33\t**Missing inputs:** the unknowns that would change the plan most, and any assumption the phase\n34\torder rests on.\n35\t\n36\t## 2. Dependency map\n37\tOnly the dependencies that bind and that the phase order does not already show:\n38\t\n39\t| What waits | Depends on | Kind | Blocked from being |\n40\t|---|---|---|---|\n41\t| … | … | decision / validation / risk-security / organizational / economic (structural or runtime only when surprising) | built / deployed / specified / hardened / exposed / committed |\n42\t\n43\tThen one line naming the kinds with no instance (\"No organizational or economic dependencies.\").\n44\tIn brownfield work, mark each dependency CONFIRMED or ASSUMED.\n45\t\n46\t## 3. Tradeoff gates (resolved up front)\n47\t\n48\t| Decision | Reversibility | Default (chosen now) | Assumption | Validated by | Flip condition |\n49\t|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n50\t| Consistency vs availability | R2/R3 + one-clause reason | … | … | V…, a cheap check, or the cited basis | … (for a gated row: \"V… fails, or …\") |\n51\t| Monolith vs services | … | … | … | … | … |\n52\t| Sync vs async | … | … | … | … | … |\n53\t| Build vs buy | … | … | … | … | … |\n54\t| Data-privacy boundary (personal or regulated data) | … | … | … | … | … |\n55\t| <each system-specific R2/R3 decision, e.g. the tenancy model> | … | … | … | … | … |\n56\t| (Brownfield) migration strategy, coexistence and cutover, rollback, system of record | … | … | … | … | … |\n57\t| (AI) prompt+RAG vs fine-tune | … | … | … | … | … |\n58\t| (AI) hosted API vs self-host | … | … | … | … | … |\n59\t\n60\t**R1 defaults:** <decision> → <default>; … (one line; no rows for R1 decisions).\n61\t**N/A:** <considered decisions that do not apply> — <reason> (one line).\n62\tOmit the (Brownfield) and (AI) rows when they do not apply. Classification and constraints\n- **What:** a local command-line tool. You give it a folder, and it renames each photo to its EXIF capture time (default `YYYY-MM-DD_HHMMSS[-NN].<ext>`). It writes an undo journal, and it previews by default: renames happen only with `--apply`.\n- **Type:** software. Greenfield. A small build: one developer, no services, no money, and personal use assumed (see Missing inputs).\n- **Dominant constraint:** correctness, meaning no photo is lost and each gets the right name.\n- **Worst failure:** a rename silently overwrites another photo. The original is gone for good. On POSIX systems `os.rename` replaces an existing target without warning, and on case-insensitive file systems `IMG_1.JPG` and `img_1.jpg` count as the same name. Close second: many files get renamed to the wrong date with no way back.\n- **Build vs buy:** you may not need to build this. `exiftool '-FileName<DateTimeOriginal' -d '%Y-%m-%d_%H%M%S%%-c.%%e' DIR` already covers a one-off job. This plan assumes you want what that one-liner lacks: preview by default, a journal with one-command undo, collision handling that is safe on case-insensitive file systems, and sidecar files kept with their photos.\n\n**Budgets**\n\n| Budget | Target | Label | Checked by |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| Data safety | 0 files lost or overwritten; undo restores every name and file hash exactly | ASSUMPTION (basis: renaming must never destroy content; confirm you never want overwrite mode) | V1 |\n| Date correctness | 100% agreement with an exiftool reference on files that have a capture date; 0 names built from malformed dates | ASSUMPTION (basis: one wrong date means one misfiled photo) | V2 |\n| Throughput | ≤ 60 s for 5,000 photos on a local SSD | ASSUMPTION (basis: only headers are read, a few ms per file) | Phase 1 exit check |\n| Resource use | Peak memory < 200 MB whatever the folder size | ASSUMPTION (basis: streaming header reads, no image decoding) | Phase 1 exit check |\n| Operational complexity | Zero services; one package installed with pipx | ASSUMPTION | n/a |\n\n**Missing inputs** (assumptions stated; none changes the phase order):\n1. **Audience.** Assumed: you and a few others, installing from a GitHub Release. If this is a public PyPI release, the build is no longer small: add release hardening (see §10).\n2. **Formats and devices.** UNKNOWN: which cameras and phones, and which of JPEG, HEIC, or RAW. You supply a sample folder before V2 can run (Phase 1).\n3. **Date meaning.** Assumed: the camera's local wall-clock time, with no timezone conversion. If you shoot across timezones and want normalized times, the §3 date-semantics row flips.\n4. **Videos.** Assumed out of scope. QuickTime stores `CreateDate` in UTC, which needs separate handling.\n\n## 2. Dependency map\n\n| What waits | Depends on | Kind | Blocked from being |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| Running `--apply` on original folders (not copies) | V1 no-overwrite and undo proof | risk/security | exposed |\n| V2 date-correctness run | Your sample folder covering every device and format | organizational | built (the gate itself) |\n| The supported-format list in docs and `--help` | V2 | validation | specified |\n| Date and timezone naming policy | Your answer to Missing input 3 (default chosen in §3) | decision | specified (Phase 1) |\n| Public release | Missing input 1 | organizational | exposed |\n\nNo economic or runtime dependencies. exiftool becomes a runtime dependency only if V2 fails.\n\n## 3. Tradeoff gates (resolved up front)\n\n| Decision | Reversibility | Default (chosen now) | Assumption | Validated by | Flip condition |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| Write-safety model | R2. It would be R3 without the seam, because an overwrite is permanent; the preview, journal, and no-clobber seam is built in Phase 0, so a wrong rename can be undone | Rename in place; preview by default; write the journal entry before each rename; never overwrite (check the target case-insensitively and reserve names within the run) | Renaming in place can be made provably reversible on NTFS, APFS, ext4 and exFAT | V1 | V1 fails on any file system → use copy mode on that file system: write renamed copies to a new folder and leave the originals untouched |\n| Date semantics | R2. A whole library may be renamed and synced before anyone notices; undo exists but copies made after the run don't follow it | Use `DateTimeOriginal` as written by the camera. Break same-second ties with `SubSecTimeOriginal`, then `-NN`. Ignore `OffsetTimeOriginal` for naming. A file with no valid date is skipped and reported, never guessed | You want the local time where the photo was taken | V2, plus your confirmation of Missing input 3 | You want UTC or home-timezone names → add `--tz`; V2 shows many photos with no date → add opt-in `--fallback mtime` |\n\n**R1 defaults:**\n- Language and distribution: Python 3.11+, a wheel built by CI, installed with `pipx`.\n- EXIF backend: pure Python (Pillow plus `pillow-heif`) behind a `DateSource` interface. If V2 fails, switch to PyExifTool for the failing formats.\n- Naming template: fixed in Phase 0; `--format` comes in Phase 2.\n- Journal format: JSON Lines with a `version` field; undo stays readable for every past version.\n- Data-privacy boundary: fully local, no network calls. Logs and journal hold only paths, timestamps and EXIF tag names, never GPS data or full EXIF dumps.\n- Build vs buy: build (see §1); flips to the exiftool one-liner if you only need a one-off rename.\n\n**N/A:** consistency vs availability, monolith vs services, sync vs async. It is a single local process working sequentially, with no shared state.\n\n## 4. Walking skeleton (Phase 0)\n- **Real request:** `photo-rename ~/tmp/copy-of-DCIM` on a disposable copy of about 200 real photos from your phone. It prints a plan (`old → new`, plus skips with reasons). Then `--apply` renames the files, and `photo-rename undo` puts every name back.\n- **Steps it runs through:** argument parsing → folder scan (top level only; symlinks not followed) → JPEG `DateTimeOriginal` read → name planner (skips any target that already exists, compared case-insensitively) → renamer with write-ahead journal at `DIR/.photo-rename/<run-id>.jsonl` → summary and exit code.\n- **Deploy:** GitHub Actions runs tests on Ubuntu, macOS and Windows; a tag builds the wheel into a GitHub Release; you install that release with `pipx install <release-wheel-url>`, as a user would.\n- **Logging and monitoring** (for a CLI, this means the result is visible to whoever runs it):\n  - a final summary of renamed, skipped and errored counts, with the run ID;\n  - `--log-file` writes JSON Lines, one line per file;\n  - exit codes: 0 = clean, 1 = some files skipped, 2 = errors.\n- **Rollback:** install the previous release wheel with pipx and confirm with `--version`. On the data side, `undo`.\n- **Who can reach it:** only you, and only on disposable copies. Running on originals waits for V1.\n- **Exit check V0:**\n  - the real folder copy is renamed and undone, and the same run ID appears in the summary, the log and the journal;\n  - a release, its install, and a rollback to the previous version all succeed;\n  - an injected truncated JPEG and an injected read-only file each show up as a reported error with exit code 2, with no other file affected;\n  - wall time and peak memory for the folder are recorded as baselines.\n\n## 5. Phases\n\n- **Phase 1: Safety and date correctness**\n  - **Unlocks:** running `--apply` on original folders (V1) and committing to a list of supported formats (V2).\n  - **Depends on:** Phase 0 / V0.\n  - **Tasks** (widest rework first):\n    1. Make the journal crash-safe: write an `intent` record and fsync it before each rename, then a `done` record after. `undo` and `resume` work out the state when an `intent` has no `done`.\n    3. Collision policy: compare names case-insensitively; reserve names within the run; add `-NN` suffixes; on file systems with hard links, rename with `link`+`unlink` so it can't clobber, and elsewhere check then rename (single user; race documented).\n    4. Parse dates strictly. Accept only `YYYY:MM:DD HH:MM:SS`; reject `0000:00:00` and anything else. Build names from parsed integers, never from raw EXIF strings, so a crafted tag can't inject `../`.\n    5. Idempotence: a file whose name is already its target is a no-op, so a second run renames nothing.\n    6. Add the date-semantics default from §3, plus reports per skip reason.\n    7. Classification and constraints\n- **What:** a local command-line tool. You give it a folder, and it renames each photo to its EXIF capture time (default `YYYY-MM-DD_HHMMSS[-NN].<ext>`). It writes an undo journal, and it previews by default: renames happen only with `--apply`.\n- **Type:** software. Greenfield. A small build: one developer, no services, no money, and personal use assumed (see Missing inputs).\n- **Dominant constraint:** correctness, meaning no photo is lost and each gets the right name.\n- **Worst failure:** a rename silently overwrites another photo. The original is gone for good. On POSIX systems `os.rename` replaces an existing target without warning, and on case-insensitive file systems `IMG_1.JPG` and `img_1.jpg` count as the same name. Close second: many files get renamed to the wrong date with no way back.\n- **Build vs buy:** you may not need to build this. `exiftool '-FileName<DateTimeOriginal' -d '%Y-%m-%d_%H%M%S%%-c.%%e' DIR` already covers a one-off job.
